mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has risen each week for three consecutive weeks (-22.0 to -20.0). This autocorrelated momentum in retail footfall reflects persistent household adaptation to current mobility conditions and should continue to push RETAIL_REC higher over the next four weeks absent a shock.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC improved monotonically from -22.0 to -20.0 over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC mean over the next 28 days is lower than or equal to the mean over the last 28 days, breaking the three-week improving streak.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT mobility has improved slowly but consistently (-38.1 to -37.1). If TRANSIT improves by more than 1.5 points week-on-week, it signals a crossing into renewed commuting/shopping trip behavior that should lift RETAIL_REC within two weeks as transit-dependent shoppers return to retail corridors.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT improves by more than 1.5 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT rose from -38.1 to -37.1 over the snapshot window
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to rise in the two weeks following a TRANSIT week-on-week improvement exceeding 1.5 points.

mechanism_narrative: When WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both show concurrent upward movement, the compounded effect of returning commuters and increased public transport use amplifies retail trip-chaining (combining commute with shopping), producing a stronger positive effect on RETAIL_REC than either series alone over four weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both rise in the same week
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES rose from -23.9 to -22.1 while TRANSIT rose from -38.1 to -37.1
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC growth over the next 28 days is no greater than growth observed when only one of WORKPLACES or TRANSIT rises, indicating no interaction effect.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL mobility has declined steadily each week (6.0 to 3.6), indicating households are spending progressively less time at home. This behavioral shift toward out-of-home activity is a leading indicator that discretionary retail and recreation trips will increase over the following four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL declined monotonically from 6.0 to 3.6 over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase over the next 28 days despite RESIDENTIAL continuing its declining trend.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility dropped sharply from 55.0 to 44.3 in the first two weeks before stabilizing near 45.0, consistent with a seasonal transition (e.g., cooling weather) that reduces outdoor park visits. This seasonal substitution effect should redirect some leisure activity toward indoor retail and recreation venues within one week.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS fell from 55.0 to 44.3 and then plateaued near 45.0
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC shows no short-term uptick in the week following PARKS stabilization at a lower plateau.

mechanism_narrative: All six series show small week-on-week changes (under 2 points) in the most recent two weeks, indicating no new policy interventions (lockdowns or reopenings) are occurring. In this steady-state policy regime, RETAIL_REC should continue its mild positive drift rather than reverse sharply.
evidence_refs: fact:all series changed by less than 2 points week-on-week in the last two observed weeks
failure_condition: A sharp reversal (>5 point drop) occurs in RETAIL_REC despite no observable change in WORKPLACES or TRANSIT exceeding 2 points, falsifying the steady-state assumption.

mechanism_narrative: If PARKS mobility were to fall below 35.0 (a drop of more than 10 points from the current 45.0 level) within the next two weeks, this would signal a tightening of outdoor gathering restrictions or a severe weather/health advisory event, which historically coincides with broader mobility retrenchment including reduced RETAIL_REC visits as caution spreads to other categories.
candidate_trigger: PARKS falls below 35.0 within two weeks
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS currently at 45.0 after stabilizing from a prior sharp decline
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC continues to rise even after PARKS falls below the 35.0 threshold, indicating no restriction-driven spillover.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM has remained essentially flat (-16.3 to -16.1) while RETAIL_REC has improved, suggesting that essential-trip behavior is saturated and any further mobility gains are being channeled specifically into discretionary retail and recreation rather than essential shopping. This divergence should persist and widen over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM stayed within a 1.3 point range while RETAIL_REC rose 2 points over the same period
failure_condition: GROCERY_PHARM and RETAIL_REC move together (both rising or both flat) rather than diverging, undermining the saturation-substitution mechanism.
